title: Computer Systems, OS, Networking & JVM
summary: Understand what the machine, operating system, network and JVM are doing underneath application code.

modules.title: Linux runtime & command line
modules.summary: Operate and inspect the environment production services run in.
modules.why: You cannot debug production systems if processes, files, signals and permissions are invisible to you.

units.title: Filesystem, permissions & environment
units.summary: Navigate Linux storage and execution context safely.
units.challenge: Create a least-privilege runtime directory structure and diagnose permission failures.
units.evidence: Shell transcript explaining every permission and ownership choice.

units.title: Shell composition & diagnostic tools
units.summary: Use pipelines to inspect and transform system state.
units.challenge: Extract a useful diagnostic report from logs/process output using only shell tools.
units.evidence: Reusable diagnostic script with explanation of each pipeline stage.

units.title: Processes, signals, ports & open files
units.summary: Inspect running services from the operating system outward.
units.challenge: Diagnose a deliberately unhealthy service without opening its source code.
units.evidence: Incident-style diagnosis using process, network and file evidence.

modules.title: Computer architecture for software engineers
modules.summary: Connect source code to CPU execution, memory hierarchy and machine representation.
modules.why: CPU caches, memory layout and instruction costs explain performance effects that Big-O alone cannot.

units.title: Binary representation & machine data
units.summary: Understand integers, floating point, characters and endianness at machine level.
units.challenge: Write programs that expose overflow, rounding and byte-order effects.
units.evidence: Annotated byte-level examples and tests.

units.title: CPU execution, instructions & cache hierarchy
units.summary: Understand pipelines and locality well enough to explain real performance behaviour.
units.challenge: Benchmark row-major vs cache-unfriendly access and a false-sharing workload.
units.evidence: Measured latency/throughput with hardware-level explanation.

units.title: Memory hierarchy & locality-aware design
units.summary: Connect object/data layout to throughput and latency.
units.challenge: Compare array-based and pointer-heavy structures under realistic access patterns.
units.evidence: Performance note separating algorithmic and locality effects.

modules.title: Processes, threads & scheduling
modules.summary: Understand execution units and why concurrency costs exist.
modules.why: Thread pools, containers and Java concurrency all depend on OS scheduling semantics.

units.title: Processes & address spaces
units.summary: Understand process isolation and execution context.
units.challenge: Inspect process trees and memory maps for a running Java application.
units.evidence: Diagram mapping a process to its memory regions and OS metadata.

units.title: Threads & context switching
units.summary: Understand shared memory execution and scheduling overhead.
units.challenge: Compare many-thread CPU and blocking workloads while observing scheduler behaviour.
units.evidence: Measurement note explaining when more threads stop helping.

units.title: Scheduling, priorities & starvation
units.summary: Reason about fairness and latency under contention.
units.challenge: Create CPU contention and explain latency changes from scheduler observations.
units.evidence: Timeline/metrics linking contention to request latency.

modules.title: Virtual memory & allocation
modules.summary: Understand pages, faults, allocation and memory pressure.
modules.why: Memory leaks, GC behaviour, swapping and container limits are easier to debug with a VM mental model.

units.title: Virtual memory, pages & translation
units.summary: Understand how virtual addresses map to physical memory.
units.challenge: Observe page faults and memory growth under controlled allocation.
units.evidence: Experiment log explaining minor/major fault behaviour.

units.title: Stack, heap & native memory
units.summary: Distinguish memory regions and ownership models.
units.challenge: Map JVM process memory to OS-visible regions.
units.evidence: Annotated process memory map.

units.title: Memory pressure, paging & OOM
units.summary: Diagnose memory exhaustion across host, container and runtime layers.
units.challenge: Trigger controlled memory pressure in a limited container and trace the failure path.
units.evidence: Root-cause report separating JVM heap, native and container memory.

modules.title: Filesystems, file descriptors & I/O models
modules.summary: Understand persistence and I/O primitives beneath files, sockets and databases.
modules.why: Database, network and logging performance eventually become OS I/O problems.

units.title: File descriptors & filesystem semantics
units.summary: Understand open files, descriptors, buffering and durability boundaries.
units.challenge: Trace file descriptor usage and demonstrate buffered vs durable writes.
units.evidence: Experiment explaining which writes survive abrupt termination.

units.title: Blocking, non-blocking & multiplexed I/O
units.summary: Understand how servers handle many concurrent sockets.
units.challenge: Compare thread-per-connection and event-loop server models conceptually or with tiny prototypes.
units.evidence: Architecture note relating I/O model to concurrency strategy.

units.title: Storage devices, latency & durability
units.summary: Reason about disks/SSDs and why sequential/random access matters.
units.challenge: Design a write-heavy persistence path under latency/durability constraints.
units.evidence: Storage choice memo with latency and durability assumptions.

modules.title: IP networking, addressing & routing
modules.summary: Understand how packets move between hosts and networks.
modules.why: Cloud VPCs, service communication and outage debugging all rest on routing fundamentals.

units.title: IP addressing, subnets & routing
units.summary: Reason about packet destination and route selection.
units.challenge: Design subnets for a small multi-tier environment and trace sample routes.
units.evidence: Network diagram plus route-table walkthrough.

units.title: NAT, firewalls & network boundaries
units.summary: Understand address translation and stateful filtering.
units.challenge: Explain why a private service can reach the internet but cannot receive unsolicited inbound traffic.
units.evidence: Packet-flow diagram with translations and filters.

units.title: Packet-level troubleshooting
units.summary: Use network tools to locate failures instead of guessing.
concepts: DNS vs connect vs TLS vs HTTP failures
units.challenge: Diagnose intentionally broken DNS, routing and port-listener scenarios.
units.evidence: Troubleshooting decision tree and captured evidence.

modules.title: TCP, UDP & transport behaviour
modules.summary: Understand reliable streams, retransmission, congestion and transport trade-offs.
modules.why: Timeouts, connection pools, HTTP performance and real-time systems all inherit transport behaviour.

units.title: TCP connection lifecycle
units.summary: Understand handshakes, sequence numbers and teardown.
units.challenge: Capture and annotate a TCP connection from handshake to close.
units.evidence: Packet trace with lifecycle explanation.

units.title: Loss, retransmission & congestion control
units.summary: Understand why latency and throughput change under network stress.
units.challenge: Introduce latency/loss and observe application-level effects.
units.evidence: Measurement note linking packet behaviour to request latency.

units.title: UDP & QUIC concepts
units.summary: Understand when applications prefer datagrams or QUIC-style transport.
units.challenge: Compare requirements for DNS-like, voice/video and request/response workloads.
units.evidence: Transport-selection matrix with failure/latency reasoning.

modules.title: DNS, TLS & HTTP protocol stack
modules.summary: Follow a browser/service request through naming, secure transport and application protocol semantics.
modules.why: Modern API and web architecture depends on understanding all three layers together.

units.title: DNS resolution & caching
units.summary: Understand recursive resolution, records and caching behaviour.
units.challenge: Trace resolution for a real domain and simulate a stale DNS-cache scenario.
units.evidence: Resolution sequence diagram and TTL analysis.

units.title: TLS, certificates & trust
units.summary: Understand server identity, key exchange and certificate validation.
units.challenge: Inspect a TLS handshake and diagnose an intentionally invalid certificate chain.
units.evidence: Trust-chain explanation and packet/tool output.

units.title: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 & HTTP/3
units.summary: Compare connection use, multiplexing and transport implications.
units.challenge: Compare network waterfall behaviour across protocol versions using browser/dev tools.
units.evidence: Protocol comparison tied to latency and connection count.

modules.title: Java concurrency & memory model
modules.summary: Write and diagnose concurrent Java with a correct model of visibility, ordering and scheduling.
modules.why: Concurrency bugs can silently corrupt data and only appear under production timing.

units.title: Thread safety, races & synchronization
units.summary: Protect shared invariants under concurrent access.
units.challenge: Reproduce lost updates and fix them with three synchronization strategies.
units.evidence: Interleaving explanation plus correctness/performance comparison.

units.title: Java Memory Model, visibility & happens-before
units.summary: Understand why code order is not always execution visibility order.
units.challenge: Build visibility/publishing examples that fail without correct synchronization.
units.evidence: JMM reasoning note showing the happens-before edges.

units.title: Executors, futures & virtual threads
units.summary: Choose concurrency abstractions based on workload shape.
units.challenge: Compare fixed pools, CompletableFuture and virtual threads for CPU vs blocking workloads.
units.evidence: Benchmark and architecture recommendation.

modules.title: JVM internals, GC & JIT
modules.summary: Understand Java execution from bytecode through allocation, garbage collection and compilation.
modules.why: JVM-level evidence separates real performance problems from folklore.

units.title: Bytecode, class loading & runtime metadata
units.summary: Understand how Java code becomes executable runtime structures.
units.challenge: Inspect compiled bytecode and demonstrate class-loader isolation.
units.evidence: Annotated bytecode and class-loading experiment.

units.title: Object allocation & garbage collection
units.summary: Understand reachability, generations and pause/throughput trade-offs.
units.challenge: Generate allocation pressure and compare GC behaviour under two collectors/settings.
units.evidence: GC/JFR report connecting allocation pattern to pauses/throughput.

units.title: JIT compilation & runtime optimization
units.summary: Understand warmup, profiling and optimization/deoptimization concepts.
units.challenge: Create a microbenchmark where naive timing produces a false conclusion, then fix methodology.
units.evidence: Benchmark methodology note explaining JIT effects.

modules.title: Systems performance diagnostics
modules.summary: Diagnose CPU, memory, I/O and contention using evidence across OS and JVM layers.
modules.why: Architect-level performance work starts with locating the bottleneck, not tuning random knobs.

units.title: CPU profiling & flame-graph reasoning
units.summary: Find where CPU time is actually spent.
units.challenge: Profile a CPU-bound Java workload and remove the dominant bottleneck.
units.evidence: Before/after profile and measured improvement.

units.title: Heap, native memory & leak analysis
units.summary: Separate leaks, retention and normal memory demand.
units.challenge: Find a seeded memory-retention bug and prove the fix.
units.evidence: Heap analysis with retaining path and post-fix measurement.

units.title: I/O, lock & saturation diagnosis
units.summary: Connect blocked time and saturation to user-visible latency.
units.challenge: Diagnose a service slowed by one of lock, DB-pool or disk contention without being told which.
units.evidence: Evidence chain from symptom to constrained resource.
